# Chachakka Sutta (MN 148 (PTS MN iii 280))

**ID:** MN 148 (PTS MN iii 280)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Chachakka Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** Six By Six
**PTS:** MN iii 280
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In Sri Lankan tradition preserved in the *Papañcasūdanī*, the celebrated preacher Maliyadeva thera famously recited the sutta across numerous vihāras (including the Lohapāsāda), each time leading sixty monks to arahantship [Adikaram 1946].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: SA 304 六六; SHT Sutta 71; Up 3.059; SN 35.60 Sabbupādānapariññāsutta
- Resembling parallels: Arv 4 Dvā-Daśāyatanāni; DN 33 (PTS DN iii 207) Saṅgīti Sutta; MN 137 (PTS MN iii 215) Saḷāyatanavibhaṅga Sutta; SĀ 323-327; SA 330 六愛身; SF 18 Chachakka; MN 38 (PTS MN i 256) Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta; MN 18 (PTS MN i 108) Madhupiṇḍika Sutta; SN 12.44 Lokasutta
- Mentioned in: Kv 6.7 Ākāsosanidassanotikathā; Mnd 11 Kalahavivādasuttaniddesa; Ne 4 Desanāhāravibhaṅga

**Sources**

- [Bendall 1893] Cecil Bendall, Catalogue of Sanskrit, Pali, and Prakrit books in the British Museum (1893) — Catalogue entry noting Chachakkasutta placement in Uparipaṇṇāsaka, Saḷāyatanavagga.
- [Roach 2014] Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach, Buddhist and Wittgensteinian Approaches Toward Language (2014) — Discussion of the sutta's analysis of self-clinging, designation, and lack of ontological status.
- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Account from the Papañcasūdanī of Maliyadeva thera preaching the sutta at Lohapāsāda and other sites.
- [Lin 2015] Qian Lin, Mind in Dispute: The Section on Mind in Harivarman's Tattvasiddhi (2015) — Comparison of the cognitive sequence in Chachakka Sutta with SĀ 304 (Ṣaṭṣatka).
- [Watanabe 1983] Fumimaro Watanabe, Philosophy and its Development in the Nikāyas and Abhidhamma (1983) — Alignment of the topics in Chachakkasutta with chapters of the Sarvāstivāda Dharmaskandha.
- [Webster 2005] David Webster, The Philosophy of Desire in the Buddhist Pali Canon (2005) — Quotation and discussion of painful feelings giving rise to underlying tendencies toward aversion.
